title: Family Apartments & Kids' Activities in Podgora 2027
metaDescription: Where to stay in Podgora with kids in 2027: apartments near gentle pebble beaches, prices in euros, day trips to Makarska and Biokovo, and local tips.
content: ## Why Podgora Works for Families Podgora is a small resort on the Makarska Riviera, located 9 km from Makarska at the foot of the Biokovo mountains. The Riviera is a 60 km strip of pebble beaches, and the entry into the water at Podgora is shallow and gradual. That makes it easier for toddlers and young swimmers than the steeper coves elsewhere on the coast. The village is compact. The main beach is lined with cafés and restaurants, the promenade is flat and shaded by palms and pines, and a local bus runs along the coast to Makarska and Tučepi. Podgora is also cheaper and quieter than Makarska, and it still has enough restaurants and ice cream shops that families do not need a car for daily life. ## Best Areas to Stay in Podgora with Kids ### Town centre and main beach The centre is the best choice for families with strollers or children under 6. Shops, pharmacies, restaurants and the beach are all within 5 minutes on foot. Evenings are lively but not loud. ### Čaklje bay Čaklje is a quieter bay on the Podgora shoreline with apartments right beside the sea, such as Letica Apartments. It suits families who want a calm pebble beach and a few waterfront restaurants rather than a busy centre. ### Upper Podgora (Stara Podgora) The old village sits on the hillside above the coast. It offers stone houses and views, but access involves steps and slopes, and the sea is a drive or a long walk away. Skip it if you travel with a stroller or a toddler. ## Family-Friendly Apartments in Podgora Self-catering is the sensible format for families here. A kitchen lets you cook early dinners for small children, and a balcony gives parents somewhere to sit once kids are asleep. - **Apartments Coast 27:** rated 9.2/10 across 159 reviews, with guests regularly mentioning stays with a baby and a 6-year-old. - **Apartments and Rooms Nikša and Apartmani Niko:** both rated 9.7/10, with balcony views of the sea and Biokovo. - **Apartments Tanja:** 200 m from the beach, from about €97 per night in high season, with air conditioning. - **Apartments Damjan:** studio and two-to-four-person units 50 m from the sea, with parking and a terrace. - **Letica Apartments:** modern units directly beside the sea in Čaklje. For families of four or five, look for two-bedroom units, since a single living-room bed is tight for children over 8. Air conditioning is essential from late June to early September, when daytime temperatures often exceed 30°C. Confirm parking when booking, because spaces in the centre fill early in July and August. ## Things to Do with Kids in Podgora ### Beaches and swimming The main Podgora beach has shallow entry, nearby cafés and toilets, which makes it the easiest option for children. Pack water shoes (about €8–12 in local shops), because pebbles are hot at midday and sharp on bare feet. Morning is the best time for toddlers, since shade is limited on the beach itself. ### Promenade and playgrounds The waterfront promenade has playgrounds near the seafront and is flat enough for scooters and strollers. Walk it at 18:00–20:00, when temperatures drop and the cafés fill. ### Water sports Watersport centres along the shoreline rent stand-up paddleboards and offer boat rides. Paddleboarding in the morning is calm, as the sea is usually flat before the afternoon breeze. ### Short hikes Trails run through pine forests and olive groves above the village toward the Biokovo foothills. Keep walks under 1–2 hours with children and start before 10:00 in summer. ## Day Trips from Podgora ### Biokovo Skywalk The Biokovo Nature Park ticket costs around €10 per adult in April–May and October, and €15 in June–September. Children under 7 enter free, and the ticket covers the road and the Skywalk. The road is narrow with sharp turns, and the temperature at the top is much cooler than at the coast, so bring a jacket. Families with children prone to car sickness should think twice. This is a drive best done in the morning. ### Aquapark Makarska The aquapark is in Makarska on Put Cvitačke, around 9 km from Podgora. It is the closest option for water slides when children outgrow the pebble beach. Check current ticket prices and opening dates with the park directly, since they change by season. ### Makarska town Makarska has a long town beach with plenty of facilities and cafés, which is a good choice for families with children. The promenade and the old centre make an easy half-day trip by bus or car. ### Island boat trips Speedboat tours from Makarska visit Brač, Hvar and a blue lagoon, typically for €70–90 per adult. Skip the full-day speedboat trips with children under 6. The rides are fast and bumpy, and the day is long. A calmer boat on a shorter route suits small children far better. ## Insider Tips for Families - **Book by February** for July and August. The best-rated family apartments sell out first. - **Shop for groceries in the morning**, before the heat. Supermarkets in Podgora are small but stocked with the basics. - **Eat early.** Restaurants serve dinner from around 18:00, and children's portions or simple pasta and grilled fish are standard. - **Choose June or September** for lower prices, warm water and fewer crowds. - **Bring beach shade.** A small umbrella or pop-up tent is worth carrying, because natural shade on the main beach is limited. ## Getting There Podgora is roughly 60 km from Split and about 1 hour by car along the coast road. Split Airport is the nearest major airport, and coastal buses link Split with Makarska and Podgora. Cars are useful for Biokovo and for beach hopping, but they are not essential for a beach-focused stay.

faq.question: Is Podgora good for families with small children?
faq.answer: Yes. The pebble beaches have a shallow, gradual entry into the sea, the promenade is flat, and the village is quiet compared with Makarska. Self-catering apartments with kitchens are common.

faq.question: How much do family apartments in Podgora cost?
faq.answer: Prices run from roughly €46 per night for small units in low season to about €100–170 in July and August. For example, Apartments Tanja starts at about €97 per night in high season. Book early for the lowest prices.

faq.question: What is the best area to stay in Podgora with kids?
faq.answer: The town centre is the most practical choice, with the beach, shops and restaurants all within a short walk. Čaklje bay is a calmer alternative with apartments right by the sea.

faq.question: Are there things to do in Podgora when it rains or is too hot?
faq.answer: Options are limited in Podgora itself, so families usually head to Makarska, 9 km away, for the aquapark and town facilities. Biokovo Skywalk is a cooler option on hot days, with tickets at €10–15 per adult and free entry for children under 7.

faq.question: Do you need a car in Podgora with children?
faq.answer: Not for a beach holiday, since most things are within walking distance and a coastal bus serves Makarska. A car helps for Biokovo, for beach hopping and for carrying gear.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Podgora with kids?
faq.answer: June and September are the best months, with warm sea, lower prices and fewer people. July and August are the hottest and busiest, so air conditioning and early booking matter most then.

quickAnswer: Podgora suits families with small children because of its shallow, gentle pebble beaches, a flat palm-lined promenade and quiet streets. Apartments with kitchens and air conditioning cost roughly €50–160 per night depending on season. Makarska, 9 km away, adds an aquapark, and Biokovo's Skywalk is free for children under 7.
